title: Ruth: loyal love in a hard time
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. lines: Ruth is set in the dark days of the judges, but it's told from inside one family in Bethlehem.
A famine drives them to Moab, and the men die there. Naomi turns for home with nothing. And her Moabite daughter-in-law won't leave her.
Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.

scripture.text: your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.

lines: The book has four chapters, and they balance. A scene on the road. A scene in the field. A scene at the threshing floor. A scene at the gate. The third is the turning point.
Naomi's emptiness in chapter one is answered by the child in her lap in chapter four.

scripture.text: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty.

lines: Watch for a Hebrew word, hesed. It names a love that keeps faith inside a relationship and goes beyond what duty requires.
Ruth shows it to Naomi. Boaz shows it in the field.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: God in ordinary days
lines: Nobody in Ruth sees a vision or a wonder. A famine ends. A harvest comes. Ruth happens to walk into the field of Boaz.
The storyteller lets you see God's hand in those ordinary turns without forcing the point.

scripture.text: under whose wings you have taken refuge.

lines: A kinsman-redeemer was a near relative responsible for protecting a family's land, name, and people when they couldn't protect themselves.
Boaz takes on that role at cost to himself.

scripture.text: The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the surprise at the end
lines: Then comes the surprise. Ruth is called the Moabitess again and again, yet she takes refuge in the LORD and becomes an ancestor of David.
He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
The small family story turns out to be a hinge in Israel's history. And Matthew names Ruth in the family line of Jesus.

scripture.text: He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.

lines: Read all four chapters in one sitting, slowly. Watch the words that keep coming back: return, empty and full, kindness, wings, redeem.
The book treats grief honestly, and it lets hope arrive slowly.
